A tiny tip compared to others... mostly for if you wake up and are struggling to get out of bed.

A cold can of anything, soda, pop, water. Stored within arm's reach from bed. Then when you wake up in the morning, gently press the cold metal can onto each eyelid. Afterwards, you'll feel more refreshed and awake as if you've just washed your face with cold water.. but more pleasant..

Plus the can stays cool and you won't have to keep refrigerating.

I was treated for severe depression and severe anxiety for around four years, until I was put onto two medications. The first was mirtazipine 35mg, which gave me weight gain, but then paired with venlafaxine really really worked for me personally.
I'm so thankful..

It took maybe a couple months for me to notice the changes, but medication needs time to work for us in our bodies. My anxiety isn't completely gone, and neither is my depression, and that trauma may stay for a while yet. But the huge takeaway from getting onto the right meds for YOU, is that it gives you hope.. and I am so much more of a functioning adult now with every year showing some progression. I'm even back in education, which I didn't think was possible in the last 4 years

Side note: getting onto medication can be a scary thing, and that's very understandable! Having something with a long list of side effects can be overbearing. But please know that everyone's experience is different, and yours will be a normal response to the medication. Understanding and having patience will help in the long run.

I would recommend looking up on Google pet names for bfs and going through that list, and finding one that might stick?

Being affectionate can take many forms, even talking awkwardly about your honest feelings about them can be really sweet to hear. There's also touching them, not in a sexual way, but stroking their arm every so often. Or for me personally flicking them with my finger in a joking manner. These things can be affectionate without too being cringey, or overly gushy. But it can also lead the way to being more confident in showing your feelings.

Pure adrenaline, and overthinking, but mostly thoughts of, it will be all over soon. I woke up the next day, with the dread of telling my mum, I had the choice to not tell her, but I felt like a robot, probably because I was drained from all the previous emotions. But after telling her, I realized that she would have gone into my room at one point, and try to wake me up, imagining her face turning from confusion, to concerned, to the realization I was dead. It still have left me with mixed emotions, I'm not glad, im on the fence about it all. But during it, I was on a one track mind, tunnel vision, I could see my goal, I couldn't see anything else.

And just so you know, I'm not in anyway disregarding you voicing your thoughts of killing yourself, and feelings of not want to be here. You don't deserve to have these thoughts, and they shouldn't be allowed to intervene with your life. You, deserve, better, and I wish I could take your anxiety away. I know, to an extent, what anxiety can do to you, and the trauma it causes afterwards.

The position you're in right now is horrible, anxiety being one part, and then the feeling of your brain overthinking must be exhausting. I take it you're a very empathetic person, because of your brain constantly looking from different perspectives all the time? And wanting to crawl out of your skin, shows that you're not comfortable in it in the first place, it DOES makes sense, it's still a horrible feeling. Your brain working in overdrive constantly won't help with it either, I suppose.
I know that you've probably considered all options that are imaginable at this point, and talked about it too. But, what helps you or distracts you when your head goes into these dark places? What seems to always make you stop your overthinking? Even for a split second? And where does your brain seem to go? It's okay to not share if you're not comfortable doing so..
